chapter: Regional bands, politics and travel abroad
title: Inviting Steven Wilson to speak
summary: Hinton asks Wilson's son Steven to join, and Steven mentions Woody Shaw and his interest in his father's trio work.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Steven, if you'd like to ask some question about something, Teddy asked a couple questions, it'd be nice to have your voice in on this oral history.
On what, exactly, just music history?
Yeah. We've mentioned about you and the rest of the family, one of the sons, and when you were born and that sort of stuff. (Inaudible).

Oh, I just came back from New York to visit my mother. And she's out -- Woody Shaw was playing the Palace. And a very good bass player named Stafford James. Excellent. The drummer was excellent, too, (inaudible). I really enjoyed that. They played until 4:00 o'clock in the morning. Started at 10:00 and played until 4:00. Of course, I couldn't stay too long.
Would you like to ask your Dad anything about yesterday? I mean yesteryear.
Yeah, well, I've always been curious about his trio work. Like when I used to hang out with you at Michael's pub. I wasn't 100 percent into jazz at the time but now that I'm really into it --
I've heard some very nice things about you (inaudible).
